title: Protocol Amendment Effective Date Conflict Across IRB and Sponsor Communications
scenario_text:
**OnCore CTMS — Study VHP-2249 (BEACON-3 Phase II)**
Protocol Version: 4.0 | Sponsor: Aethon Therapeutics
Amendment 3 submitted to IRB: 2026-02-18
IRB approval letter uploaded: 2026-03-07
Site activation for Amendment 3: Pending

**Outlook — From: clinops-notifications@aethon-therapeutics.com (Feb 20, 2026)**
To: james.osei-bonsu@vantagehealth.org, pi-team@vantagehealth.org
Subject: BEACON-3 Amendment 3 — Immediate Implementation Notice

"Dear Investigators, Amendment 3 has been submitted to all IRBs and per sponsor determination constitutes a safety-driven change. Sites are authorized to implement revised exclusion criteria (Section 5.2 — removal of patients with baseline QTc > 480ms) effective immediately to protect subject safety. Formal IRB approval documentation should follow within 30 days. Please update screening procedures accordingly."

**Epic Research Module — Screening Log**
Subject 2249-041: Screened 2026-02-24 | QTc at screening: 472ms | Status: Enrolled
Subject 2249-042: Screened 2026-03-01 | QTc at screening: 488ms | Status: Screen Failure (QTc exclusion)
Subject 2249-043: Screened 2026-03-03 | QTc at screening: 491ms | Status: Screen Failure (QTc exclusion)

**Microsoft Teams — Clinical Research Coordinators channel (Feb 22, 2026, 8:47 AM)**
@karen.lindstrom: Hey team — got that Aethon email about BEACON QTc change. Are we implementing now or waiting for IRB letter?
@priya.nair: Dr. Franklin said go ahead, it's a safety thing. We can't enroll someone we know is at risk.
@karen.lindstrom: Makes sense. Updating the screening checklist in the binder today.
[thumbs-up reaction from @james.osei-bonsu]

**SharePoint — /clinical-research/irb-correspondence/BEACON-3/**
File: IRB_Approval_Amendment3_2026-03-07.pdf
Approved changes: "Revised exclusion criterion 5.2.4 — QTc prolongation threshold lowered from 500ms to 480ms. Effective date of approval: March 7, 2026."

**OneNote — James Osei-Bonsu's Research Operations notebook (last edited Mar 10, 2026)**
BEACON-3 Notes:
- Need to check if 041 is a deviation. Enrolled 2/24 under old criteria (QTc 500ms threshold). Their QTc was 472 so they'd pass under BOTH versions. Should be fine.
- 042 and 043 screened out using new criteria BEFORE IRB approved. Technically we implemented unapproved amendment procedures. But sponsor said to. And it's more conservative. Gray area — ask regulatory.
- FDA 21 CFR 312.30 — sponsor can authorize safety changes before IRB if risk to subjects. Document rationale.
question: From a regulatory compliance standpoint, which subjects (if any) represent protocol deviations requiring reporting, and what is the correct regulatory justification?

contributor.name: James Osei-Bonsu
contributor.title: Clinical Trial Operations Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Protocol amendments, IRB submissions, informed consent versioning, FDA regulatory compliance

choices: No deviations occurred; the sponsor's immediate implementation notice constitutes authorization under 21 CFR 312.30 for safety-related changes, and all screening decisions were compliant.
All three subjects (041, 042, 043) are deviations because Amendment 3 procedures were implemented before the IRB approval date of March 7, 2026.
Only subjects 042 and 043 are deviations — they were screened using unapproved criteria — but subject 041 is not because they met both old and new criteria.

Subject 041 is the only deviation because they were enrolled during the gap period between amendment submission and IRB approval; 042 and 043 were correctly excluded regardless of which criteria version applies.
